title: docs(types): state the object-grid operations ceiling on rowActions and operations
body:
Fixes #10084

Clause-②: no

## What changed

Text only. No member is added and no behaviour changes.

- `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`: `ObjectGridSchema.rowActions` had no describe. It now has one.
- `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`: the `ObjectGridSchema.operations` and `rowActions` docblocks now state how the two keys combine. The `update` / `delete` member docs dropped `@default true`. That default is not what the runtime does: a declared block withholds any member it does not name.
- `.changeset/10084-grid-ceiling-describe.md`: `@object-ui/types` patch.

The texts describe exactly what `resolveRowCrudAffordances` in `packages/plugin-grid/src/rowCrudAffordances.ts` does on `main` at `142fdfd`, together with its call site in `ObjectGrid.tsx`. That behaviour landed in two PRs: objectui#10081 (ceiling) and objectui#10228 (narrowing). It implements ruling batch 162, item 1, letter A on objectui#9819.

- `operations` is the ceiling. `operations.update: false` / `delete: false` withholds that generic row entry whatever `rowActions` says. So does a member that a declared block does not name, because a present block replaces the wired-callback default.
- A declared `rowActions` list narrows. It offers the generic Edit / Delete only for the canonical `edit` / `delete` names it carries. This applies to `[]` and to a list that names only custom actions.
- An absent `rowActions` keeps the default.
- Non-canonical names are custom actions resolved against the object's declared actions.

`ObjectGridSchema` in zod still declares no `operations` member. It is admitted through `.passthrough()` only, and adding one is out of scope (see re-measure comment 5808437270).

## Pinning tests

None pin these texts. How I searched:

- `git grep -n` found the old docblock strings `Custom row actions` / `Enable/disable built-in operations` only in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, never in a test or script.
- No test reads `ObjectGridSchema.shape.rowActions`. Positive control: `object-grid-export-options-refusal-7762.test.ts` reads `ObjectGridSchema.shape.exportOptions.description`, and the same grep finds it.
- No generated artifact carries grid describe text. `Enabled operations` appears only in `objectql.zod.ts`.

## Gates (head `914f272`; `origin/main` did not move, so the merge was a no-op)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check`: exit 0. The dependency closure has no build script (`ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT`), so there was nothing to build.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/`: 213 files, 4919 tests passed.
- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts`: 1 file, 199 tests passed.
- `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` on the 2 changed source files: 0 errors. 35 `no-explicit-any` warnings, none inside the changed hunks. The config has no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions` / `projectService`), so the diff cannot move the verdict for any untouched file.
- `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`: exit 0.
- `pnpm check:new-line-citations`: exit 0, 0 new citations.
- Control-byte self-scan of the 3 files: no hits.

## Acceptance notes (observations only, nothing filed)

- The `operations.create` / `read` member docs still say `@default true`. On `object-grid`, `showAddRow` reads `!!operations?.create`, and the default block holds only `update` / `delete`, so create is off when the block is absent. I left this alone because it is outside the ceiling ruling. Carrier: none.
- The `object-grid.operations` entry in `registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` has `pins` prose that still says `update` / `delete` are "a UNION with `rowActions`". That has been stale since objectui#10081. It is ledger prose and no assertion reads it. Carrier: none.
- The `GRID_QUERY_INPUTS` descriptions of `rowActions` / `operations` in `packages/plugin-grid/src/index.tsx` also leave the ceiling unstated. That is a second author-read surface, and it is outside this card's granted file surface. Reported to the dispatch seat.
